desk.headline: Revenue up 45% to $9.55bn, adjusted EPS $5.06 vs $3.04, beat; full-year guidance raised to $12.50–12.80
results: Revenue rose 45% to $9.55bn, mainly from the Calpine gas fleet bought in January, and topped the $9.35bn estimate.

Adjusted operating EPS jumped to $5.06 from $3.04 (estimate $3.88), helped by Calpine, strong trading and higher capacity prices, partly offset by lower nuclear tax-credit revenue and higher interest.
The nuclear fleet ran at a 97.2% capacity factor (99.2% over summer), with output slightly above last year.

New deals: a 20-year, 690 MW supply deal with Amazon at Calvert Cliffs, a 20-year deal with Google funding ~890 MW of uprates, a $715m Rhode Island gas plant purchase and a conditional DOE loan commitment of up to $5bn.
About $3.0bn of shares bought back so far this year; operating cash flow for nine months was $4.98bn.

guidance.summary: Full-year 2026 adjusted operating EPS guidance moved up to $12.50–12.80 from $11.50–12.50, the second raise this year; the new low end equals the old top end.

points: Management called this a record contracting year, with more than 8,500 MW of long-term agreements signed so far.
It launched Peak+, pairing nuclear supply with new capacity or demand response, priced against new gas plants.
Roughly 1,200 MW of nuclear uprates costing about $4.3bn are planned, mostly online 2029–2032; the DOE loan could cut interest costs.
The CFO cautioned that this year's trading outperformance may not repeat every year.
2027–2028 guidance and an updated buyback plan will come with Q4 results; management expects regulatory clarity on co-location in 2027.
